name: Defense Health Agency
description: DoD's combat support agency for the Military Health System. Buys MHS GENESIS, PEO DHMS / EIDS, enterprise imaging, and the cyber and data modernization layer beneath them.
mmtRead: DHA reorganized April 20, 2026 with FOC target July 19. PEO DHMS retains executive authority over MHS GENESIS, JOMIS, and DMIX/EIDS while acquisition reporting moves under AD-RDA. The Office of Warfighter Health Advantage (RDML Tracy Farrill, just appointed) consolidates data, analytics, AI, and digital health into a single seat. The HCDS deployment RFP and the Leidos bridge are both inside the PAE transition window.
procurementSignals: HCDS deployment RFP (inside PAE transition window)
PEO DHMS Deployment Solutions HT003826RE001 ($300M, proposals due Apr 21 2026)
Leidos bridge ~$1.4B sole-source (competition delayed to 2028 earliest)

at_risk: EHRM funding (30% withheld pending June 1 conditions)

current_read: DHA reorganized April 20, 2026. Two senior seats Acting (Arena at AD-RDA; Soliz at HCAO); RDML Tracy Farrill just seated at OWHA. PEO DHMS reporting moves under AD-RDA but executive authority over MHS GENESIS / JOMIS / DMIX-EIDS does not transfer. FOC target is July 19. The HCDS deployment RFP and the Leidos bridge are both inside the PAE transition window.
upcoming_signals: PAE Medical Software & Business Systems lead assignment (Key Next Step)

name: Department of Veterans Affairs / Veterans Health Administration
description: Largest integrated healthcare system in the US (1,298 facilities, 9M+ enrolled veterans). VHA delivers care; VA OIT runs the IT layer through T4NG2 and IHT 2.0; community care flows through CCN Next Gen; imaging and ambient AI are active growth areas.
mmtRead: VA EHR modernization is back on track with four Michigan sites live April 11, 2026 — first wave of 13 sites planned for 2026. T4NG2 is awarded ($60.7B, 33 final awardees post-protest). IHT 2.0 ($14B, 100% SDVOSB, 9 awardees) covers VHA technology services through 2035. The VA Ambient Scribe IDIQ (36C10B26R0006) is in active GAO protest with decision due Aug 6 2026.
procurementSignals: CCN Next Gen Medical 36C10G26R0003 (proposals closed Apr 3 2026)
VA Ambient Scribe protest decision due Aug 6 2026
VA Health Services DevSecOps 36C10B26Q0163 sources sought
current_read: VA executed CCN Next Gen procurement (proposals due Apr 3 2026, currently in award review). EHRM Michigan wave went live Apr 11 2026 (first 4 of 13 planned sites). T4NG2 awarded with 33 final roster after protest resolution. The VA Ambient Scribe IDIQ has an open GAO protest (B-424447.1, decision Aug 6 2026).
key_offices: VA OIT (Office of Information and Technology)
upcoming_signals: VA Ambient Scribe protest decision Aug 6 2026

name: Department of Health and Human Services
type: Cabinet Department (parent of CMS, NIH, FDA, CDC, IHS, ONC, ARPA-H)
description: Department-level map. HHS itself sets policy and coordinates; the buying happens through its operating divisions. Map: CMS (Medicare, Medicaid, claims), NIH (research IT, NITAAC), FDA (Sentinel, regulated-product data), CDC (data modernization, DCIPHER), IHS (PATH EHR), ONC (interoperability, certification), ARPA-H (OTA-funded R&D).
mmtRead: HHS IT spend is decentralized. Treat HHS as a navigation layer: route procurement questions to the operating division that owns the program (CMS for claims, NIH for research IT, FDA for surveillance, etc.). The departmental level is for policy and rulemaking, not contract awards.
procurementSignals: See operating division profiles for actual procurement
openVehicles: See CMS / NIH / NITAAC for operating-division vehicles
current_read: HHS at the department level coordinates policy. Buying flows through CMS, NIH, FDA, CDC, IHS, ONC, and ARPA-H. Use the operating-division profiles for actual procurement opportunities.
key_offices: Operating Divisions (CMS, NIH, FDA, CDC, IHS, ONC, ARPA-H)

name: Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT
type: HHS Sub-Office (regulatory, not a primary buyer)
description: Sets health IT interoperability standards, certifies EHR technology under ONC Health IT Certification, owns USCDI evolution, runs TEFCA implementation through the RCE (Sequoia Project), and enforces information blocking under 45 CFR Part 171.
mmtRead: ONC's procurement footprint is small. Its regulatory leverage is enormous: USCDI determines what data EHRs must exchange, TEFCA determines who participates in the network, and information blocking enforcement determines who pays the penalty. Track ONC for what it enables, not what it buys.

at_risk: ONC budget is small and vulnerable to broader HHS cuts

current_read: ONC is enforcing TEFCA and expanding USCDI. Information blocking enforcement actions are increasing. ONC procurement is limited but its regulatory decisions shape billions in private-sector and government health IT spending.

name: Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health
description: Newest federal health research agency (est. 2022). Funds breakthrough health technology through Other Transaction Authority (OTA) and ISO-style program structures. Accessible to non-traditional vendors through program-manager-led solicitations.
mmtRead: ARPA-H's procurement model is the access lever. OTA awards are not constrained by FAR-style competition rules, which is why non-traditional vendors and academic-industry teams can win. Watch ADVOCATE (agentic clinical AI), Sprint for Women's Health, and the next program announcement wave for FY2027.
procurementSignals: Sprint for Women's Health solicitation rolling
FY2027 budget zeroed in HHS proposal — executing on existing FY2026 funds

budget.fy2027_request: Zeroed in proposed budget (executing FY2026 funds)
at_risk: FY2027 budget zeroed in HHS proposal

current_read: ARPA-H is executing first wave of major programs. ADVOCATE awards expected June 2026. OTA model accessible to non-traditional vendors.

name: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
type: HHS Operating Division (largest single payer in US)
description: Administers Medicare, Medicaid, CHIP, the ACA Marketplace, claims processing systems, and program integrity infrastructure. Largest single payer in the US healthcare system. CMS modernization runs through SPARC and a network of multi-year IDIQs.
mmtRead: CMS procurement is large-scale and long-cycle. SPARC ($25B, POP through Jun 7 2026) is approaching recompete. Claims modernization, payment integrity, and AI fraud detection are the active growth areas. The Rural Health Transformation program ($50B FY2026-FY2030) is grant funding to states, not a contract.
procurementSignals: Rural Health Transformation grant cycle (state awards)
current_read: CMS executing SPARC recompete preparation and advancing data modernization. AI fraud detection and payment integrity are growth areas. The Rural Health Transformation Program is grant-funded ($50B FY2026-FY2030 to states), not a contract.
key_offices: CCIIO (Center for Consumer Information and Insurance Oversight)
OAGM (Office of Acquisition and Grants Management)

name: Indian Health Service
description: Federal health system serving American Indian and Alaska Native populations. Currently executing PATH EHR Modernization on Oracle Cerner / Oracle Health to replace the legacy RPMS system. Vendor: GDIT.
mmtRead: IHS PATH is the active EHR modernization arc — replacing RPMS with Oracle Health on the GDIT platform. Tribal health IT procurement intersects with both federal contracting and tribal sovereignty considerations, which constrains what vendors can compete and how.
keyPrograms: PATH EHR Modernization (Oracle Health, GDIT prime, RPMS replacement)
current_read: PATH is the active modernization. Tribal sovereignty considerations shape competition.

name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
description: Federal public health agency. Buys data modernization, surveillance, and analytics tooling through DMI, PHDS, DIBBs, and DCIPHER (Palantir Foundry-based). State, tribal, local, and territorial (STLT) adoption of DIBBs tools is a tracked metric.
mmtRead: CDC's procurement focus is data modernization. DMI is the umbrella; PHDS is the data services layer; DIBBs is the toolkit; DCIPHER is the Palantir-based surveillance platform. The 2026 target is greater than 30 percent STLT adoption of at least one DIBBs product.
procurementSignals: DIBBs STLT adoption acceleration (2026 target greater than 30 percent)
current_read: CDC is driving DIBBs adoption at the STLT level and continuing DCIPHER expansion on Palantir Foundry.
key_offices: CSELS (Center for Surveillance, Epidemiology, and Laboratory Services)
Office of Public Health Data, Surveillance, and Technology

name: Food and Drug Administration
description: Regulates food, drugs, biologics, devices, and tobacco. Buys post-market surveillance and regulated-product data systems through Sentinel, market-research vehicles, and operating-division IT modernization. Sentinel 3.0 market research is active (75F40126SSN00100).
mmtRead: FDA Sentinel is the flagship post-market drug surveillance program. Sentinel 3.0 is in market-research stage with eight tiers spanning data broker services (1-6), GOCO platform (Tier 7), and scientific support (Tier 8). NAICS 518210.
procurementSignals: Sentinel 3.0 sources sought 75F40126SSN00100 (closed Mar 23 2026; full RFP expected 2026)
current_read: Sentinel 3.0 market research active. Eight-tier scope across data, platform, and scientific support.

name: National Institutes of Health / NIH IT Acquisition and Assessment Center
description: NIH is the country's biomedical research agency. NITAAC is NIH's acquisition center and runs CIO-SP3 / CIO-SP4 (canceled) / CIO-CS — the NIH GWACs that anchor IT procurement across HHS. Treat NIH as both a research buyer and an acquisition channel for the rest of HHS.
mmtRead: CIO-SP4 was canceled (SAM Amendment 0017 on RFP 75N98121R00001). CIO-SP3 is the active bridge through Apr 29 2027. CIO-CS is the IT commodities vehicle and a follow-on (`The Store`) is in pre-RFP at a reported $20B-$25B.
current_read: CIO-SP4 canceled. CIO-SP3 bridges through Apr 29 2027. CIO-CS follow-on in pre-RFP.

name: General Services Administration
description: Acquisition channel only. GSA runs Alliant 3 (active, no ceiling), Polaris (small business), 8(a) STARS III ($50B), and OASIS+ (governmentwide professional services). Track GSA vehicles for the access lane, not for the agency mission itself.
mmtRead: Alliant 3 went live with NTP March 10 2026 (42 Phase 1 contractors). Polaris small business GWAC is active. 8(a) STARS III ordering window runs through Jul 1 2026 with GSA option through 2029. OASIS+ continues on-ramping.
procurementSignals: 8(a) STARS III ordering window closes Jul 1 2026
current_read: Track GSA vehicles for the access lane, not the agency mission.
